properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 10:01PM PDT until October 11 at 1:00AM PDT by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Imperial County in southeastern California...

* Until 100 AM PDT.

* At 1001 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Algodones Dunes, Gordon's Well and Andrade.

This includes CA Interstate 8 between mile markers 70 and 81.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 AM PDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
SVRPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
East Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* Until 1015 PM MST.

* At 952 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles southeast
of Dateland, or 41 miles west of Gila Bend, moving north at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Paloma, Dateland and Sentinel.
properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 9:43PM PDT until October 11 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning through Sunday afternoon,
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is likely. For
the Beach Hazards Statement from Sunday morning until Sunday
evening, surf of 5 to 7 feet with local sets up to 9 feet. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday
afternoon, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and beach boardwalks may be closed due
to high water. Low-lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may flood during morning high
tides. Beach erosion. Elevated surf will lead to a high risk of
rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on Sunday morning from
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel with a combination of increased
swell, onshore winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High
tides lower each day into the middle of the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:

possible.

* WHERE...Portions of North Carolina, including the following areas,

Virginia, including the following areas, Carroll, Floyd, Grayson

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

debris.

Valley, periods of rain will continue. Heavier rainfall will
continue in short bursts through the day. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1 to 3 inches, along with what has already fallen will
keep the threat of flooding around.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Burke, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:24AM EDT until October 11 at 6:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Burke County in western North Carolina...

* Until 615 AM EDT.

* At 1224 AM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady
rainfall produced 3-6 inches across Burke County, saturating area
soils.  Doppler radar shows several rounds of torrential rainfall
have moved through the area from the south, capable of producing
1.5-3 inches of rainfall on top of saturated soils.  This rainfall
will cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.

* Areas of greatest concern include along Hunting Creek near
Morganton; poorly draining areas of Morganton and other urban areas
along US 70; Silver Creek south of Glen Alpine; and Henry and Jacob
forks of the South Fork Catawba River near South Mountains State
Park.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only 12 inches
of water can strand your vehicle or sweep it away.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Morganton, Longview, Valdese, Salem, Icard, Drexel, Hildebran,
Connelly Springs, Rutherford College and Glen Alpine.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 9:17PM PDT until October 11 at 12:15AM PDT by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Imperial County in southeastern California...

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 917 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
El Centro, Calexico, Brawley, Imperial, Holtville, El Centro
Naval Airfield, Mt. Signal, Heber, Alamorio, Seeley and Bonds
Corner.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; San Diego County Inland Valleys; San Bernardino County Mountains; Riverside County Mountains; San Diego County Mountains; Apple and Lucerne Valleys; Coachella Valley; San Diego County Deserts; San Gorgonio Pass Near Banning
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 9:16PM PDT until October 11 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southwest California, including the following
areas, Apple and Lucerne Valleys, Coachella Valley, Riverside
County Mountains, San Bernardino County Mountains, San Diego County
Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County
Mountains, San Diego County Valleys and San Gorgonio Pass near
Banning.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel will bring periods of moderate to
heavy rain to all of San Diego County, Riverside County mountains
and deserts, and San Bernardino County mountains and deserts
through late Sunday afternoon. Maximum hourly rainfall rates of
0.50 to 0.60 inches per hour are possible for San Diego Coast and
Valleys. Maximum hourly rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.70 inches per
hour are possible across area deserts and 0.70 to 1 inch per hour
rates are possible across area mountains. Heaviest rainfall is
most likely through early Sunday afternoon. Rainfall will taper
off from south to north Sunday. Lingering lighter showers are
expected to continue into Monday.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 9:09PM PDT until October 12 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. Short
period north-northwest wind waves will interact with a
building west-northwest long period swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday afternoon. The
risk will be highest during Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Ashe, NC; Watauga, NC; Wilkes, NC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 12:06AM EDT until October 11 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Ashe County in northwestern North Carolina...
Watauga County in northwestern North Carolina...
Southwestern Wilkes County in northwestern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1205 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1.5 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Watagua River, Laurel Fork, Flat Branch, Norris Fork, Meat Camp
Creek, Elk Creek, Left Prong Stony Fork, Dugger Creek, Grassy
Creek, Mill Creek, Brushy Fork, Little Dugger Creek, Fall Creek
and Dutch Creek. Additional rainfall amounts up to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Boone, Blowing Rock, Deep Gap, Todd, Foscoe, Seven Devils and
Aho.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.
